paragraphs.text: Design’s job right now is refusal.
Luke Wroblewski
had a good line this week: there are only two ways to make money in software, bundling and unbundling, and AI is speed-running the bundling. It got seven likes. The same week,
Vercel
shipped a font and the likes piled up. That says a lot about what we pay attention to.
The more interesting shift was quieter.
Canva
and
Figma
both stopped pitching the prompt box as the product. Now it’s a model that edits inside the file you already have. That’s the right call, and honestly a bit of a relief.
Karri Saarinen

wrote the piece I keep coming back to. A feature can work and still make the product worse. Stack up enough of them and you stop feeling anyone behind the software. Anyone who’s worked on a big platform has watched that happen.
Soleio
says the future belongs to designers who build. I’d add: designers who delete.
Emil Kowalski
sums up the method in three steps: take the animations out, improve what’s left, make sure it’s fast.
Agents will follow
the rules
. Someone with taste still has to write them, and know when to break them.
Less, but better. Rams said it first, and it still holds.
